entries.title: The Nature of Memory
entries.text: Memory is not storage. Memory is *structure*. The world does not exist in atoms or energy, but in the shared remembering of all conscious beings. When the last mind forgets a thing, that thing ceases to have ever existed.

entries.title: The First Fracture
entries.text: It began with a single forgotten name. A child's imaginary friend. A lover's promise. A dying word unheard. The fracture spread like a crack in glass, each forgotten thing weakening the whole. By the time the great civilizations noticed, half the world was already gone.

entries.title: The Memory Walkers
entries.text: Some souls are born with the gift - or curse - of walking between memories. They see the fractures. They can enter the memories of others, navigate the spaces between recollections, and pull lost things back into existence. They are the Memory Walkers. You are one.

entries.title: The Ruins Civilization
entries.text: The first to fall. They built their cities from memory-stone, believing permanence was possible. Their archives held the names of every citizen, every deed, every love and loss. When the fracture came, the stone forgot its shape. The archives became labyrinths of blank pages. The Scavengers are their descendants, driven mad by the silence where memories should be.

entries.title: The Whispering Forest
entries.text: The forest-dwellers chose a different path. They bound their memories to living wood, letting the trees remember for them. For centuries it worked - the forest grew dense with recollection. But when the fracture reached the roots, the trees began to *misremember*. They grew memories that never happened. The Wildlings are those who lost themselves in the false growth. The Spirits are the forest itself, trying to prune the corruption.

entries.title: The Echoing Caves
entries.text: Deep below, the cave-dwellers discovered that sound carries memory better than stone or wood. They sang their histories in vast chambers, letting echoes preserve what minds could not. The crystals grew in resonance with their songs, each facet a frozen note. But the fracture silenced the songs. The Cave Dwellers hunt by sound now, desperate for any echo of the past. The Crystal Golems are the songs given form, mindless and eternal.

entries.title: The Prism Gardens
entries.text: The most advanced civilization. They learned to *refract* memory - splitting single recollections into spectrums of perspective, storing each angle in crystal lattices. Their gardens were libraries of infinite viewpoint. But refraction requires a source light. When the fracture dimmed the sun of shared memory, the prisms turned dark. The Crystal Guardians tend dead gardens. The Prism Entities are memories that shattered into their component perspectives, each believing itself the whole truth.

entries.title: The Void Between
entries.text: Where do forgotten things go? Not to nothingness - nothingness is a concept, and concepts require memory. They go to the Void Between, the space where unremembered existence accumulates. It is not empty. It is *full* of things that never were, because no one remembers them being. The Void Walkers are the antibodies of reality, erasing the unremembered to prevent infection. The Forgotten are the memories that refused to die, clawing their way back from non-existence.

entries.title: The Sanctuary and the Keeper
entries.text: At the center of all fractures lies the Sanctuary. It is not a place - it is the *possibility* of a place. The Keeper tends it. Some say the Keeper was the first Memory Walker. Some say the Keeper *is* the collective memory of all walkers. The Keeper does not guard the Sanctuary. The Keeper *is* the Sanctuary. To reach it is to understand: reconstruction is not restoration. It is creation.

entries.title: The Truth of Reconstruction
entries.text:
You have walked the fractures. You have gathered the pieces. You stand at the Altar of Reconstruction. Now you must choose:

1. RESTORE: Return the world to what it was. Safe. Familiar. But the fracture remains in the foundation. It will happen again.

2. REFORM: Keep the memories, change the structure. A new world from old pieces. The fracture becomes a feature, not a flaw.

3. REBIRTH: Release all memories. Let the world forget completely. From true nothingness, a truly new world can grow. But you will not be in it.

4. TRANSCEND: Become memory itself. Join the Keeper. Guide future walkers. Never rest. Never end.

There is no wrong choice. There is only *your* choice. And the world will remember what you decide.

entries.title: Memory Fragments
entries.text: Fragments are the currency of reconstruction. Each piece contains a sliver of lost reality - a color, a sound, a feeling, a fact. Alone, a fragment is meaningless. Combined, they form Core Memories: pivotal moments that unlock new abilities and reveal the path forward. The Primordial Memory is the theoretical complete set - the memory of the world's first moment. No walker has ever assembled it. Perhaps you will be the first.

entries.title: The Cycle
entries.text: Scholars of the Prism Gardens calculated: the fracture is not a disaster. It is a *cycle*. Memory accumulates. The world becomes rigid, overdefined, brittle. The fracture is the world breathing out, releasing what it no longer needs. Reconstruction is breathing in. The walkers are the lungs. Each run is a breath. The world has breathed countless times. It will breathe countless more. Your run is one breath. Make it meaningful.

entries.title: The First Remembering
entries.text: The Keeper guarded a lantern, not a tomb. Beneath its light the first name is still being spoken, and every section the walker restores is an answer. The First Memory is not a monster. It is the question the world asked before it had a word for asking.

fragment_001.text: The taste of rain on hot stone.

fragment_003.text: The weight of a sword you never lifted.

fragment_005.text: The name of the first forgotten thing.

fragment_012.text: A map of the fracture's first path.

fragment_015.text: The last words of the Ruins' king.

fragment_042.text: The song that makes trees walk.

fragment_055.text: The first note of the cave-song.

fragment_067.text: The crystal that grew from a tear.

fragment_089.text: A memory seen from seven angles.

fragment_101.text: The prism that split the self.

fragment_150.text: The sound of a memory dying.

fragment_200.text: The name of the first Forgotten.

fragment_500.text: The cycle completes. The cycle begins.

fragment_071.text: The foreman's last order: keep the line moving.

fragment_072.text: A brass heart with a human name stamped inside.

fragment_073.text: The swamp repeats every name it swallows.

fragment_074.text: A crown of reeds, still warm from a head that drowned.

fragment_081.text: The comb hums in shifts. Nobody told it the shift ended.

fragment_082.text: A worker's name, written in wax and rewritten every morning.

fragment_083.text: The catacombs keep rank. The first keeper still expects a report.

fragment_084.text: A bone tag: WALKER, FIRST OF THE SANCTUARY. The rest is worn away.

fragment_tide_01.text: Bell buoys rocking on black water, ringing for ships that never come.

fragment_tide_02.text: The blademaster's salute: sword reversed, offered to the drowned, then raised.

fragment_tide_03.text: Salt in the mortar. The harbor was rebuilt seven times and the sea took it seven times.

fragment_storm_01.text: The vanguard's oath, shouted into the gale so the mountain itself could witness.

fragment_storm_02.text: A warlord's cloak, too heavy with medals to lift in the wind, left folded on the rampart.

fragment_storm_03.text: Lightning keeps striking the same spire. The order calls it approval.

fragment_tide_04.text: A harbor manifest, every line stamped PAID, every ship named for someone loved.

fragment_tide_05.text: The blademaster's students carved their names into the pilings so the sea would remember the forms.

fragment_storm_04.text: A recruit's letter, unsent: the wind took the ink before it dried, twice.

fragment_storm_05.text: The spire bell rings thirteen times at every changing of the guard. Nobody admits casting it.

fragment_first.text: Before the first name, there was only the wish to be remembered.

core_memory_001.title: The First Walker
core_memory_001.text: She walked when the world was whole. She saw the first crack. She tried to mend it with her own memory. She became the first fracture.

core_memory_002.title: The Stone That Forgot
core_memory_002.text: They built eternity from memory. Eternity lasted three generations. The fourth generation found only dust and blank books.

core_memory_003.title: The Tree That Lied
core_memory_003.text: The oldest tree remembered a forest fire that never happened. The fire became real. The forest burned. The tree survived.

core_memory_004.title: The Silent Song
core_memory_004.text: The last singer sang the song of ending. The crystals wept. The echoes still carry the melody in the deep dark.

core_memory_005.title: The Prism's Truth
core_memory_005.text: A memory has no single truth. It has as many truths as there are minds to hold it. The prism does not distort. It reveals.

core_memory_006.title: The Void's Purpose
core_memory_006.text: The Void is not the enemy. The Void is the womb. Every forgotten thing gestates there. The Forgotten are not monsters. They are the next world waiting to be born.

core_memory_007.title: The Work That Continued
core_memory_007.text: The foundry never learned the world had ended. It kept making parts for a city no one would assemble. The swamp kept repeating the names of the workers. Between the two, a kind of memory survived: not a person, not a place, only the habit of continuing.

core_memory_008.title: The Habit of Going Out
core_memory_008.text: Before the Sanctuary had walls, it had a rota. Before it had a rota, it had one walker who went out every morning and came back with a name. The hive inherited the shift. The catacombs inherited the rank. The Sanctuary inherited the habit of going out again.

core_memory_009.title: The Sunken Tideways
core_memory_009.text: The harbor was rebuilt seven times, and seven times the sea took it. The blademasters still salute the drowned; the bell buoys still ring for ships that never come. Salt is in the mortar, names are in the pilings, and every manifest is stamped PAID. What the tide keeps, it keeps with names.

core_memory_010.title: The Howling Spire
core_memory_010.text: The order built its spire where the lightning already struck, then called the strikes approval. The vanguard shouts its oath into the gale; the warlord's medal-heavy cloak waits folded on the rampart; the bell rings thirteen times at every changing of the guard. The wind keeps what the ink cannot.

core_memory_011.title: The First Remembering
core_memory_011.text: The first name was not a word. It was a promise that someone would come back for it. The First Memory has been waiting under the Keeper's lantern ever since, repeating the promise until a walker answers.

primordial_memory_001.title: The Primordial Memory
primordial_memory_001.text:
In the beginning, there was only Memory.
And Memory said: 'I remember.'
And there was World.

And Memory said: 'I forget.'
And there was Void.

And Memory said: 'I reconstruct.'
And there was Walker.

And Memory said: 'I choose.'
And there was Ending.

And Memory said: 'I begin again.'
And there was... 

[The rest is yours to write.]
